clue.text: They might offer a sea view

definitions.text: They might offer a sea view

parts.words: They might offer a sea view
parts.note: a bay is an inlet of the sea, so the clue playfully suggests windows looking out over one, though the term really names a projecting style of window

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase names an architectural feature, a window projecting outward from a wall; the sea-view reading comes from 'bay' as a coastal inlet.
explanation.definitionFit: Projecting windows of this style give a wide outlook, and a 'bay' is also a curving stretch of coast, hence the sea view.

clue.text: Book everyone spirited enough for soccer, for example

parts.note: everyone means all
game describes someone plucky and willing enough to have a go

explanation.surface: Someone reserves a lively whole-group outing to play football.
explanation.definitionFit: Soccer is one example of a sport played with a ball, a two-word phrase for any such contest.

clue.text: Delivery from northern city to our monarch?

parts.note: York is a cathedral city in the north of England
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the British queen's royal cipher

explanation.surface: A parcel is being sent from York to the King or Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Delivery' is a cricket ball: a yorker is bowled to pitch right at the batsman's feet.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a delivery is a single ball bowled, and this name is for one aimed at the batter's toes.

clue.text: Area in which one hundred step up

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word for step is read from the bottom upward

parts.note: a pace is a single step

explanation.surface: Someone describes a region where a hundred people step forward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Area' looks like part of the surface's location phrase, but it is the definition; 'up' works because this is a down entry, read from the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: A polar ice sheet is an expanse of frozen land, a geographical region covered permanently by ice.

clue.text: A peer's odd rambling made him a criminal

indicators.note: rambling means wandering aimlessly, so the letters of these words are jumbled into a new order

parts.note: the possessive s counts as a letter here

explanation.surface: An eccentric nobleman's wandering ways turned him into a lawbreaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rambling' rearranges the letters of A PEERS ODD.
explanation.definitionFit: A desperado is a reckless outlaw, the bandit figure of Wild West stories.

clue.text: Who noses around in this sort of footwear?

indicators.note: around signals that the letters of who and noses are moved about into a different order

explanation.surface: A riddle about a nosy person poking about in particular boots.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark covers the semi-literal reading: someone nosy might poke about in such boots; 'around' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A snowshoe is a broad racket-shaped frame worn underfoot to walk on deep drifts.

clue.text: A few drops of the hard stuff

definitions.text: A few drops of the hard stuff

parts.words: A few drops of the hard stuff
parts.note: suggests a nip of spirits, but the drops are frozen pellets falling from the sky

explanation.walkthrough: 'the hard stuff' is slang for strong liquor, but here it is literally hard: ice falling as precipitation.
explanation.definitionFit: These are balls of ice falling from storm clouds, literally hard drops of precipitation.

clue.text: The predicament of a very popular lake?

parts.note: something hot is in great demand
a lake is a body of water

explanation.surface: A well-loved lake finds itself in trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in trouble is an idiom phrased as being immersed in scalding liquid.

clue.text: What's implied by union split about closure

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go around the word for closure
split means broken apart, so the letters of union are rearranged

parts.note: an end is a closure or conclusion

explanation.surface: A trade union breaks up over a factory being shut down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' places the shuffled union letters (from 'split') around the closure word, leaving four letters before it and one after.
explanation.definitionFit: An innuendo is an indirect hint or insinuation, something suggested rather than said outright.

clue.text: Bulky sentries outside start to expect generosity

parts.note: bulky means large
the SS began as a protection squadron of guards, so sentries gives SS

indicators.note: start to means only the first letter of expect is used

explanation.surface: Large guards outside are waiting for some open-handed giving.
explanation.walkthrough: SS, Hitler's Schutzstaffel, began as a guard unit, hence 'sentries'; 'outside' puts them around the letter from 'start to'.
explanation.definitionFit: Largesse is liberal giving of money or gifts, open-handed bounty.

clue.text: Unfashionable home game originally meant a trip

parts.note: out means no longer in fashion
in means at home

indicators.note: originally means the first letter of game is taken

explanation.surface: A dull home fixture was supposed to be an excursion.
explanation.definitionFit: An outing is an excursion or day out, a short pleasure journey.

clue.text: Weapons creating terrible dangers across the west of England

indicators.note: across means the scrambled letters stretch over the following letter, containing it
terrible suggests something badly mangled, so the letters of dangers are scrambled
in an across clue the west of a word is its leftmost, first letter

explanation.surface: Dreadful hazards are spreading over western England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terrible' turns DANGERS into GRENADS, and 'across' places it around E, the westmost letter of 'England'.
explanation.definitionFit: Grenades are small bombs thrown by hand, a kind of explosive munition.

clue.text: She's outside now, in dark glasses

indicators.note: outside means the letters of she's are placed around the word for now

parts.note: the words are taken as written, the apostrophe ignored
AD, anno domini, marks the present era

explanation.surface: She has gone outdoors at the moment, wearing sunglasses.
explanation.walkthrough: AD (anno domini, the present era) stands for 'now'.
explanation.definitionFit: Shades is informal slang for sunglasses.

clue.text: Platform for a management buy-out

parts.note: MBO is the business abbreviation for a management buy-out

explanation.surface: A stage is being set up for executives buying their own company.
explanation.definitionFit: An ambo is a raised reading desk or pulpit in early churches.

clue.text: One may be on it at the cash dispenser!

definitions.text: One may be on it at the cash dispenser!

parts.words: One may be on it at the cash dispenser!
parts.note: bread is slang for money, and a line is a queue, so the queue at a cashpoint is jokingly given the name for poverty

explanation.walkthrough: To be on this is to be very poor; the clue reads it literally as a queue for money.
explanation.definitionFit: It names the level of income at which people are only just surviving, originally a queue for free food.

clue.text: A telephone might be hired

definitions.meaning: a phone line in use gives a busy tone
taken on, as of a worker given a job

explanation.definitionFit: The word means busy, as a phone in use, and also taken on, as an employee given a post.

clue.text: Able to figure out menu — and the price!

indicators.note: out signals that the letters of menu are put out of order

parts.note: a rate is a price or charge

explanation.surface: A diner tries to make sense of the menu and what it costs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges MENU into NUME; 'figure' belongs to the definition, not to 'figure out'.
explanation.definitionFit: Numerate means competent with numbers, the arithmetic counterpart of literate.

clue.text: Last on is hoping to contain surprise

indicators.note: to contain means the answer lies within the run of letters in last on is hoping

explanation.surface: The final performer on stage hopes to spring an unexpected twist.
explanation.definitionFit: To astonish is to amaze, to strike with wonder.

clue.text: Put at risk in final, and see red

parts.note: a final is an end or conclusion
to see red is to feel anger

explanation.surface: Losing your temper in a cup final could jeopardise everything.
explanation.definitionFit: To endanger is to expose to harm or peril.

clue.text: Censure soldier with convincing evidence

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, are British army soldiers
proof is evidence that convinces

explanation.surface: A trooper is reprimanded once the facts against him are clear.
explanation.walkthrough: RE stands for the Royal Engineers, a British army corps.
explanation.definitionFit: A reproof is a rebuke or reprimand.

clue.text: A loose grasp of property tenure?

parts.note: loose means free
a grasp is a hold

explanation.surface: Someone has only a slack grip on who owns a building.
explanation.definitionFit: Freehold is outright ownership of land or buildings, as opposed to leasing them.

clue.text: American refusal to exercise?

parts.note: the US slang word for no, read as two parts, no plus PE (physical education), gives a refusal to do exercise

explanation.walkthrough: PE is physical education, school exercise; 'refusal' serves both the definition and the joke, so this is a cryptic definition.
explanation.definitionFit: This is informal American slang for no, a casual negative reply.

clue.text: A new spirit and a condition of the heart

parts.note: gin is a spirit

explanation.surface: Someone takes up a new spirit and develops heart trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Angina is chest pain caused by restricted blood flow to the cardiac muscle.

clue.text: Sleep better embracing worker uprising

indicators.note: embracing means the word for better wraps around the next piece

parts.note: to cap something is to better or outdo it

indicators.note: in a down clue, uprising means the word for worker is read upward

parts.note: an ant is the classic worker insect

explanation.surface: Bosses think rest beats a revolt by the workforce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'better' is a verb here, to top or outdo; 'uprising' reads the insect upward since this is a down entry, and 'embracing' holds it inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A catnap is a short light doze.

clue.text: Reason out why a woman married abroad

indicators.note: out means the letters of reason are worked out into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone tries to puzzle out why a woman wed overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: Señora is the Spanish title for a married lady, equivalent to Mrs.

clue.text: Eastern gallery welcomes study lacking teeth

indicators.note: welcomes means the first pieces take in the next one

parts.note: the Tate is the famous London art gallery
a den is a private study

explanation.surface: An eastern art gallery invites in a study group without dentures.
explanation.walkthrough: The gallery is the Tate in London; 'welcomes' means the study word is taken in after the compass letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Edentate is a zoological term for animals with few or no front teeth, such as anteaters and sloths.

clue.text: Call on father to be bold

indicators.note: on means the word for call is placed after the word for father

parts.note: da is an informal word for dad
to ring is to call on the phone

explanation.surface: Phoning your dad takes some courage.
explanation.definitionFit: Daring means brave and adventurous, willing to take risks.

clue.text: Sanctimonious, with no time perhaps for a fruit

parts.note: pi is informal shorthand for pious or sanctimonious

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters of no time could be arranged some other way

explanation.surface: A self-righteous person, too busy to stop, might grab something to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: A pimiento is a sweet red pepper, botanically the fruit of a capsicum plant.

clue.text: A girl's husband after a wager

indicators.note: after means the letter for husband comes behind the word for wager

parts.note: a bet is a wager

explanation.surface: A woman's spouse follows her after placing a bet.
explanation.definitionFit: Beth is a female first name, short for Elizabeth.

clue.text: A local government may be beaten by speed

parts.note: rate means speed
capped means outdone or beaten

explanation.surface: A town council may be overtaken by fast-moving events.
explanation.walkthrough: In 1980s Britain, central government capped the local property tax (the rates) that councils could levy.
explanation.definitionFit: This British term described councils whose local tax levels were limited by central government.
